claim.text: And in the last three months of 2025, it was down to 1.7 percent.
claim.context: But in 12 months, my administration has driven core inflation down to the lowest level in more than five years. || And in the last three months of 2025, it was down to 1.7 percent. || Gasoline, which reached a peak of over $6 a gallon in some states.

row.reasoning: Every government/wire measure of Q4 2025 core inflation (core CPI ~2.7%, core PCE ~2.7-3.0%, Q4 annualized ~2.7-2.8%) contradicts the claimed 1.7% figure.

evidence.snippet: [2026-01-13] Official BLS CPI release for Dec 2025 (final month of Q4); core CPI ran ~2.7% annual, 0.2%/mo — not 1.7%.
[2026-02-20] BEA Dec 2025 Personal Income & Outlays: core PCE (ex food & energy) rose 3.0% year‑over‑year in Dec 2025, not 1.7%.
[2026-02-20] BEA advance Q4 2025 GDP release: quarterly core PCE price index rose ~2.7-2.8% annualized, contradicting a 1.7% figure.
[2026-02-20] BEA PCE data page (Feb 2026 release) shows core PCE ~3.0% YoY in December 2025, contradicting 1.7%.
[2026-02-20] BEA landing page for the Q4 2025 advance GDP/PCE estimate; core PCE annualized ~2.7%, well above 1.7%.
FRED series for Core CPI (All Items Less Food & Energy) historical data.
BEA official core PCE (ex food/energy) data page — primary series to derive the Q4 2025 three-month annualized rate.
[2026-01-22] FRED series for PCE excluding food & energy (BEA data) shows December 2025 core PCE roughly 3.0% YoY, inconsistent with 1.7%.
[2025-12-18] Nov 2025 CPI report with core YoY at 2.6%; covers Q4 start.
[2025-11-03] Treasury Q3 2025 report: core CPI ~3.0% YoY, monthly ~0.3%; no 1.7%.
